title: Control of the cell cycle and cancer; Chromosomes, karyotypes and genome organisation
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: CD05a#t1 term and clue written for the game; CD02b#t2 term and clue written for the game; CD05a#t2 term and clue written for the game; CD02b#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: CD02b#N.4, CD05a#N.2c, CD02b#N.11, CD05a#N.4b, CD05a#N.8.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Histones
items.clue: Proteins around which the DNA of a linear chromosome is wound

items.label: Tumour suppressor gene
items.clue: Its protein slows division, repairs DNA or triggers cell death

items.label: Eukaryotes
items.clue: Organisms that keep most of their DNA in a nucleus, as several linear chromosomes

items.label: Proto-oncogene
items.clue: Normal part of the genome whose protein stimulates division when the cell is signalled

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes how mutations in genes that control the cell cycle lead to uncontrolled cell division?

options.text: Mutations make both proto-oncogenes and tumour suppressor genes over-active, so both kinds of gene then stimulate division more strongly.
A mutation can turn a proto-oncogene into an oncogene that drives division, or stop a tumour suppressor gene restraining division.
An oncogene is a gene that a healthy cell does not possess, so uncontrolled division can begin only when one is introduced from outside.
Mutations in cell-cycle genes occur in gametes, so uncontrolled division appears only in the offspring that inherit the mutated gene.

questions.explanation: Proto-oncogene products promote the cycle; a mutation can make one an overactive oncogene. Tumour suppressors restrain it; disabling them removes the restraint. Either way, division is uncontrolled.

questions.stem: The model represents three levels of packing of DNA in a eukaryotic chromosome. Based on the model, which statement correctly describes the role of histones?

options.text: Histones are sections of the DNA molecule that carry some of the chromosome's genes.
Histones hold the two strands of the DNA together by pairing with its bases.
Histones change the order of the bases so that the DNA fits inside the nucleus.
Histones are proteins that DNA winds around, packing the DNA into a shorter structure.

questions.explanation: The model shows the DNA double helix wound around histone proteins, and this wound DNA is folded further into a condensed chromosome. Histones package a long DNA molecule into a compact one.

questions.stem: In chronic myeloid leukaemia, a mutated gene in blood-forming cells makes an overactive protein that keeps the cells dividing. A drug that blocks this protein stops most of the cancer cells dividing. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: The mutated gene is a tumour suppressor gene, and the drug restores its brake on division.
The drug works because it kills every dividing cell, since cancer is just fast division.
The mutated gene is an oncogene; the drug blocks the protein that drives division.
The mutated gene came from a virus, and the drug removes the foreign gene from the cells.

questions.stem: A line of eukaryotic cells grown in a laboratory carries a mutation that greatly reduces the amount of histone protein the cells make. Which prediction about the DNA in the nuclei of these cells is best supported?

options.text: Its DNA will be less tightly packed, so its chromosomes will be less condensed.
Its DNA will have a changed base sequence, as histones set the order of its bases.
Its two DNA strands will come apart, as histones hold the base pairs together.
Its chromosomes will lose some genes, as histones are sections of the DNA.

questions.explanation: Histones are the proteins that DNA winds around to become condensed. With far fewer histones, less DNA can be wound and packed, so the chromosomes are expected to be less condensed.

questions.stem: Each chromatid of human chromosome 1 contains one DNA molecule about 85 mm long. When the cell divides, the condensed chromosome is about 10 µm long (illustrative round value). Which statement is correct?

options.text: The DNA is about 8.5 times longer than the chromosome, because it is wound round histones and coiled further.
The DNA is about 8 500 times longer than the chromosome, because it is wound round histones and coiled further.
The DNA is about 8 500 times longer than the chromosome, because packing removes bases to shorten the molecule.
The DNA is about 8 500 times longer than the chromosome, because the double helix twists tighter with no proteins involved.
